description: H-1 (High, top priority): the two WebSocket routes bypass post-erasure session revocation. The HTTP guard (app.ts requireSession) verifies the session AND denies any session issued at/before an erasure cutoff via sessionInvalidation.isRevoked(claims.sub, claims.iat). But /signaling and /asr/stream authenticate through security/ws-auth.ts authenticateWs, which only calls verifySession and NEVER consults sessionInvalidation. So after DELETE /me/data, a still-valid bearer (inside its 30-min absolute window) can open a live Ring signaling session and an Amazon-Transcribe-billing ASR relay. Close this authorization gap and add a regression test. This is a self-contained backend change: one commit for the fix+test.
steps: Make authenticateWs revocation-aware in backend/src/security/ws-auth.ts. Preferred approach: change the signature to async and accept the SessionInvalidationPort, e.g. `export async function authenticateWs(request, secret, allowedOrigins, sessionInvalidation): Promise<SessionClaims | null>` — keep the Origin check first (return null when Origin not allowed), then `const claims = verifySession(extractWsToken(request), secret); if (!claims) return null; if (await sessionInvalidation.isRevoked(claims.sub, claims.iat)) return null; return claims;`. Import the SessionInvalidationPort type from ../services/session-invalidation.js. Keep extractWsToken and isOriginAllowed exactly as they are (do not regress MED-34: no token in URL query, Origin allowlist).

Update backend/src/routes/signaling.ts: the handler calls `const claims = authenticateWs(request, sessionSecret, wsAllowedOrigins)`. Change it to `const claims = await authenticateWs(request, sessionSecret, wsAllowedOrigins, app.container.sessionInvalidation)`. The @fastify/websocket handler callback is synchronous; make the handler body able to await by wrapping the auth+close in an async IIFE or by making the websocket handler callback async. Preserve the EXACT existing unauthorized behavior: on null claims, setImmediate(() => { safeSend typed error {type:'error',code:'unauthorized',...}; socket.close(SIGNALING_CLOSE.unauthorized=4401,'unauthorized'); }). Do not change any other close code or control-frame shape.

Update backend/src/routes/asr.ts the same way: `const claims = await authenticateWs(request, sessionSecret, wsAllowedOrigins, app.container.sessionInvalidation)` with the handler able to await. Preserve the exact existing unauthorized path: setImmediate(() => { safeSend {type:'error',code:'unauthorized',...}; socket.close(ASR_CLOSE.unauthorized=4401,'unauthorized'); }). Keep all HIGH-22 resource guards (liveByResident cap, maxDuration, replay) untouched.

If making the websocket route callback async is awkward with the current @fastify/websocket typing, an acceptable equivalent is to keep authenticateWs returning claims (sync verifySession + Origin) and add the isRevoked check inline in each WS handler right after authenticateWs returns non-null: `if (await app.container.sessionInvalidation.isRevoked(claims.sub, claims.iat)) { <same 4401 close path>; return; }`. Choose whichever keeps the diff smallest and the types clean; document the choice in the commit message. Either way both /signaling and /asr/stream MUST refuse a revoked (pre-erasure) bearer with the 4401 close path.

Add a regression test mirroring the existing HTTP erasure deny-list test ('DELETE /me/data invalidates existing sessions (HIGH-23 deny-list)' in backend/test/routes/transcripts.test.ts). Put WS assertions in the existing WS test files (backend/test/routes/signaling.test.ts and backend/test/routes/asr.test.ts) or a new backend/test/routes/ws-erasure.test.ts. The test must: (a) issue a session for a resident via sessionFor(sub, secret) and authorize the resident for a device (persist Ring token + deviceAccountStore.map) as the signaling tests do via their authorize() helper; (b) call `await t.container.sessionInvalidation.revokeSessionsIssuedBefore(sub, Date.now())` (or drive DELETE /me/data via app.inject so the real eraseAll path runs) with a tiny delay so the pre-erasure session's iat is <= cutoff; (c) connect the pre-erasure bearer to /signaling (via WS_SESSION_PROTOCOL_PREFIX) and assert the socket closes with SIGNALING_CLOSE.unauthorized (4401); (d) connect the same bearer to /asr/stream and assert the socket closes with ASR_CLOSE.unauthorized (4401). Use the existing ws.ts helpers (connect via sec-websocket-protocol, collectUntilClose). Because iat is epoch ms and revocation is iat <= cutoff, ensure the test revokes with a cutoff >= the session's iat (issue session, then revoke with Date.now() a couple ms later, matching how the HTTP test sleeps 2ms before DELETE).

Also add a positive-control assertion in the same test: a session issued AFTER the erasure cutoff still authenticates on /signaling (reaches the offer/answer path) so the fix does not over-revoke. This mirrors the HTTP test's 'session issued after erasure sees empty feed' intent.

Run backend typecheck, lint, and the full vitest suite; confirm all green including the new test. Verify the new test actually fails if the isRevoked check is removed (reason about it: without the check, authenticateWs returns valid claims for the pre-erasure bearer and the socket would proceed to offer handling / ASR start rather than closing 4401).
acceptance_criteria: authenticateWs consults sessionInvalidation.isRevoked after verifySession and returns null (leading to a 4401 close) for a revoked session, while preserving the Origin allowlist and the no-token-in-URL rule.
Both /signaling and /asr/stream close a pre-erasure (revoked) bearer with close code 4401 and the typed {type:'error',code:'unauthorized'} frame.

A new regression test erases a resident (or revokes sessions issued before now) then asserts a pre-erasure bearer is refused with 4401 on BOTH /signaling and /asr/stream; a post-erasure session still authenticates on /signaling.
backend npm run typecheck, npm run lint, and npm run test all pass, with the test count increased by the new WS erasure test(s).
No existing WS behavior (MED-34 Origin check, HIGH-22 guards, 4409/4408/4500 close codes) is regressed.
verification: export PATH=/opt/toolchains/.nvm/versions/node/v22.23.3/bin:$PATH && cd backend && npm run typecheck && npm run lint && npm run test
findings:
Closed the H-1 WS post-erasure authorization gap. Chose the preferred approach (async authenticateWs taking SessionInvalidationPort) so both WS routes share one revocation-aware auth path mirroring app.ts requireSession.

Changes:
- backend/src/security/ws-auth.ts:57-69 - authenticateWs is now async and accepts a SessionInvalidationPort (imported from ../services/session-invalidation.js at line 4). After the Origin check (unchanged) and verifySession, it returns null when sessionInvalidation.isRevoked(claims.sub, claims.iat) is true (line 66). extractWsToken and isOriginAllowed are untouched (MED-34 no-token-in-URL and Origin allowlist preserved).
- backend/src/routes/signaling.ts:55-66 - the /signaling websocket handler callback is now async and awaits authenticateWs(..., app.container.sessionInvalidation). The exact 4401 unauthorized close path (setImmediate -> typed {type:'error',code:'unauthorized'} frame -> socket.close(SIGNALING_CLOSE.unauthorized, 'unauthorized')) is preserved; no other close code (4408/4409/1011/1000) changed.
- backend/src/routes/asr.ts:76-87 - the /asr/stream handler callback is now async and awaits authenticateWs(..., app.container.sessionInvalidation). The exact 4401 close path is preserved and all HIGH-22 guards (liveByResident cap, asrMaxSessionMs duration cap, replay) are untouched (4429/4408/4500 unchanged).

Test added: backend/test/routes/ws-erasure.test.ts (4 tests, mirroring the HTTP 'DELETE /me/data invalidates existing sessions (HIGH-23 deny-list)' test in transcripts.test.ts). It (a) issues a pre-erasure session via sessionFor and authorizes the device (ringTokens.persist + deviceAccountStore.map); (b) revokes via container.sessionInvalidation.revokeSessionsIssuedBefore(sub, Date.now()) after a 2ms delay, and in one case drives the real DELETE /me/data via app.inject; (c) asserts the pre-erasure bearer closes 4401 on /signaling (SIGNALING_CLOSE.unauthorized) with the typed unauthorized frame and opens no session; (d) asserts 4401 on /asr/stream (ASR_CLOSE.unauthorized); plus a positive control that a session issued AFTER the cutoff still reaches the /signaling answer path (no over-revocation).

Fail-without-fix confirmation: removing the isRevoked line from ws-auth.ts and running the new file made the 3 revocation tests fail (collectUntilClose timed out at 5s because the socket never closed 4401), while the post-erasure positive-control test still passed. Source restored and re-verified.

Verification (export PATH=/opt/toolchains/.nvm/versions/node/v22.23.3/bin:$PATH && cd backend): npm run typecheck PASS, npm run lint PASS, npm run test PASS = 37 files / 279 tests (baseline was 36 files / 275 tests; +4 from the new WS erasure file). Committed as Suleiman in one atomic commit (4b09469) with no AI co-author trailer and no em/en dashes.
